q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is scheduled for August 26, 2026. Today is August 17, 2026. **9 days remain.**

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

NVIDIA has **already provided guidance** for Q2 FY2027 at $91.0 billion ±2%, which translates to a range of **$89.2 billion to $92.8 billion**. This is explicitly stated in the research provided from the company's official Q1 FY2027 earnings release.

The question asks what NVIDIA's forward guidance will be in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release. The guidance appears to have already been issued (in the prior quarter), so the company will likely reiterate or slightly adjust this figure when they report Q2 results on August 26.

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will guide approximately **$91.0 billion ± 2%** for Q2 FY2027 when they make their official announcement in 9 days.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- **Weakening demand signals**: If pre-orders or customer communications suggest slower-than-expected Blackwell adoption or delays in Rubin ramp
- **Macro deterioration**: Economic slowdown reducing AI capex spending
- **China export restrictions tightening**: Further regulatory constraints beyond current guidance already excluding China data center compute
- **Supply chain disruptions**: Manufacturing or logistics issues impacting shipment volumes
- **Conservative guidance practice**: NVIDIA typically guides conservatively; they might lower guidance if they want high confidence in hitting targets

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- **Better-than-expected Rubin demand**: UBS noted potentially 500,000 Rubin GPUs/month, faster than anticipated
- **Blackwell acceleration**: Continued strong adoption could exceed base guidance
- **Data center demand strength**: Customers front-loading orders to secure allocations
- **China regulatory clarity**: If restrictions are eased, allowing inclusion of China revenue
- **Upside surprise from other segments**: Gaming, professional visualization, or automotive exceeding expectations
- **Market competition dynamics**: If competitors face delays, NVIDIA could capture incremental demand

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research explicitly states:
- NVIDIA's already-issued guidance for Q2 FY2027: **$91.0 billion ±2%** ($89.2-$92.8B range)
- Analyst consensus: **$91.846 billion**
- UBS bullish case: **$94-95 billion actual Q2 revenue** with **$107-108 billion guidance for Q3 FY2027**

The guidance range provided in this question (99.5-115.5B) is substantially higher than the already-issued guidance, suggesting this may be asking about Q3 FY2027 guidance (to be provided during the Q2 earnings call) rather than Q2 guidance itself. The UBS case for Q3 guidance ($107-108B) would align more closely with this range.

**Interpreting the question as asking about Q3 FY2027 guidance** (typically provided during Q2 earnings call):
- Base case would be in line with UBS's $107-108B estimate
- The range 99.5-115.5B appears reasonable for forward guidance 2 quarters out
- UBS suggests strong Rubin ramp could support higher end of range

## Final probability distribution

Given the ambiguity, I'm interpreting this as Q3 FY2027 forward guidance (the forward quarter guidance issued during the Q2 earnings call):

**Low (10th percentile): 102000000000**
**Median (50th percentile): 108000000000**
**High (90th percentile): 114000000000**

This centers on the UBS estimate of $107-108B while allowing for the possibility of stronger (up to $114B) or more conservative (down to $102B) guidance based on demand signals and macro conditions at the time of the August 26 call.
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 earnings release, covering the quarter that ended July 26, is scheduled for August 26, 2026. The company has already provided guidance for Q2 FY2027, expecting revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/), [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors). This guidance does not include any Data Center compute revenue from China [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm), [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027/).

Analysts' consensus revenue estimate for Q2 FY2027 is slightly higher at $91.846 billion [hudson-labs.com](https://www.hudson-labs.com/research/nvidia-q2-2027-earnings-preview-nvda-revenue-guidance-key-factors). UBS, however, is predicting Q2 FY2027 revenue of $94-95 billion, and anticipates NVIDIA will guide for the October quarter (Q3 FY2027) to be $107-108 billion. This bullish outlook is driven by steady demand for Blackwell and an unexpectedly fast ramp-up of the next-generation Rubin platform, with Rubin shipments potentially reaching 500,000 GPUs per month [aliteq.com](https://aliteq.com/nvidia-q2-fy27-earnings-preview-ubs-2026/).
